decisions.reason: The citrus crate is a publicly presented flagship tied to the sustainability direction, so management stays committed and treats any absence from the website as a presentation change rather than failure.
The multi-model foldable large container line carries substantial tooling investment and sits at the core of returnable logistics, so the firm persists with it.
The stackable crates are a core portfolio line with sunk mold costs, and weak visibility can be attributed to pandemic-era demand disruption.
Rackable pallets are a staple offering with invested multi-model tooling, which argues for keeping them despite limited observed results.
The spill-retention pallets are somewhat peripheral but had their own page and several models, so the visible commitment favors persistence.

This single pallet variant with load retainers is the least embedded product, but its sunk mold costs and dedicated page make the firm likely to keep it and attribute weak results to the 2020–2021 disruptions.
